style_block: Warm archival documentary photography style evoking early-to-mid twentieth-century Texas oil country and 1980s American primetime and daytime television production, shot on grainy film stock, soft sepia-toned grading in the earliest scenes that gradually shifts warmer and more saturated moving from the 1930s toward the 1980s, gentle vignette, soft chromatic aberration at frame edges, subtle film scratches and dust, period-accurate wardrobe and set design, oil derricks and boxcars and dusty Texas rail yards in the earliest scenes, wood-paneled boardrooms, opulent ranch-style mansions, television soundstages and studio control rooms in the later scenes, cinematic 16:9 composition framed like a classic documentary about American business and broadcasting history. All people depicted are archetypal, fictionalized, stylized figures representative of their era and role rather than an exact reproduction or likeness of any real actor or real named individual. No modern technology, no smartphones, no flat screen displays, no exact photographic likeness of any real person, no photorealistic reproduction of real world logos or trademarked packaging text, no watermark, no signature, no extra fingers, no distorted limbs, no garbled or misspelled lettering, no text anywhere in the image.

characters.DIGGER: an archetypal 1930s-1940s Texas wildcatter character, stylized and fictionalized rather than an exact likeness of any real actor, weathered face, wire-thin build, wearing a battered felt hat and dust-covered work clothes, an expression of quiet, simmering resentment
characters.JOCK: an archetypal Texas oil patriarch character, stylized and fictionalized rather than an exact likeness of any real actor, broad-shouldered, silver-haired, wearing a tailored western-cut suit and a wide felt hat, a confident, commanding bearing
characters.CLIFF: an archetypal underdog businessman character, stylized and fictionalized rather than an exact likeness of any real actor, slicked dark hair, an ill-fitting suit that always looks slightly too eager, an expression caught between hope and exasperation
characters.JR: an archetypal ruthless oil-executive character, stylized and fictionalized rather than an exact likeness of any real actor, sharp Western-style suit, a wide confident grin that reads as more predatory than warm, always positioned as the most composed person in the room
characters.STEFANO: an archetypal wealthy, cultured European-styled businessman-patriarch character, stylized and fictionalized rather than an exact likeness of any real actor, dark tailored suit, silver-tipped cane, a calm unreadable expression that never fully reveals what he is thinking
characters.ROMAN: an archetypal plainclothes American police-detective character, stylized and fictionalized rather than an exact likeness of any real actor, rumpled sport coat, tired but alert eyes, the bearing of someone used to being underestimated

reference_notes: Same vintage film/TV grain, era-accurate documentary treatment used on the prior channel video, carried forward for visual consistency. Palette and set dressing shifted to this video's settings: Texas oil fields and ranch mansions for the Dallas story, DiMera-mansion opulence and Salem police-department interiors for the Days of Our Lives story.
